title: Foreign Death Penalty Offences (Preventing Information Disclosure) Bill 2015
short_title: Foreign Death Penalty Offences (Preventing Information Disclosure) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would criminalise certain disclosures by current or former public officials that result in someone facing investigation, prosecution, trial or punishment for a foreign death-penalty offence.
A conviction for the disclosure offence would carry a mandatory minimum prison term of one year, while courts would retain discretion over the minimum non-parole period.
The offence would exclude foreign cases involving terrorism or violence causing death or endangering life, and the legislation would begin the day after Royal Assent.
changes: The legislation would apply to conduct occurring beyond Australia.
Its geographic coverage would include every Australian external territory.
The Crown would be bound by the legislation but could not itself be prosecuted.
summary.affected: Current and former public officials and people exposed to foreign death-penalty proceedings through their disclosures are affected.
